title: Maximum Number of Accepted Invitations
summary: Given an m x n grid indicating boy-girl invitation possibilities, determine the maximum number of accepted invitations where each boy can invite at most one girl and each girl can accept at most one invitation.
statement: Given an m x n grid indicating boy-girl invitation possibilities, determine the maximum number of accepted invitations where each boy can invite at most one girl and each girl can accept at most one invitation.
constraints: grid[boy][girl] is one exactly when that invitation is possible.
Each boy and girl may participate in at most one accepted invitation; maximize the count.
hints: This is maximum bipartite matching between boys and girls.
For each boy, recursively search for an augmenting path, allowing a currently matched boy to move.
Use a fresh visited-girl set for each augmentation attempt.
Every successful augmentation increases matching size by one; when no path exists, the standard augmenting-path theorem proves the matching maximum.
editorial: Every successful augmentation increases matching size by one; when no path exists, the standard augmenting-path theorem proves the matching maximum.

tests.explanation: A reassigned augmenting path matches all three boys.
At most three girls are reachable and all three can be matched.
